LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 7.3.1 TENSE:

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense:

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense:. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What are you doing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify sentences featuring future continuous tense in print and digital texts
2. use future continuous tense in oral and written contexts correctly

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 7.3.1 TENSE:
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 7.3.1 TENSE:
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify sentences featuring future continuous tense in print and digital texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify sentences featuring future continuous tense in print and digital texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify sentences featuring future continuous tense in print and digital texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense:”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify sentences featuring future continuous tense in print and digital texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use future continuous tense in oral and written contexts correctly

What this means
In this part you learn to use future continuous tense in oral and written contexts correctly. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use future continuous tense in oral and written contexts correctly.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use future continuous tense in oral and written contexts correctly. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense:”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify sentences featuring future continuous tense in print and digital texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: to a partner. (skill: use future continuous tense in oral and written contexts correctly)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify sentences featuring future continuous tense in print and digital texts.
3. Practise this skill: use future continuous tense in oral and written contexts correctly.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense:: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense:?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are you doing?
2. What were you doing yesterday?
3. What will you be doing tomorrow?
4. How do you show an action will take place tomorrow or at a later time?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Tense: means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify sentences featuring future continuous tense in print and digital texts.
5. Be able to: use future continuous tense in oral and written contexts correctly.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
